subject: Post-call: ACME Health model qualification & structured-output conformance
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@acmehealth.com>, Sam Walters <swalters@techprocure.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed next steps (model fit + schema conformance)

Hi Priya & Sam —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have alignment before the follow-up demo: 

Summary of needs
- Primary use case: structured extraction from patient intake forms + short clinical summaries (JSON output required)
- Quality constraints: >95% key-field recall on structured fields, clear audit trail for each generated field
- Reliability constraints: p95 latency < 350ms for 512-token requests, retriable on transient failures

Redwood recommendations (shortlist for eval)
- Candidate models to evaluate: redwood/titan-7b-q4f16 (cost-efficient baseline), meta/llama3-13b-instruct (higher quality on clinical phrasing), redwood/xl-13b-quant (balanced latency/quality).
- Run initial pass with titan-7b-q4 and llm3-13b-instruct for prompt-set A (attached)

Evaluation plan and conformance checks
- Benchmarks we will run: token-level latency (p50/p95), per-field precision/recall, schema validation rate (percentage of outputs that pass JSON Schema v2). Link to ephemeral benchmark results: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmarks/acme-20270421
- Prompt sets: attached acme_prompt_set_v1.json (30 representative prompts + edge cases)
- Schema: attached acme_schema_v2.json. We will test with both strict and lenient validation modes.
- Tool/function calling: where available, we will instrument function calls for exact field extraction (e.g., call: extract_patient_record(payload) -> JSON). We'll simulate both direct JSON outputs and function-call routing to validate failure modes.
- Retries & graceful degradation: plan to test automatic retry on transient 5xx and fallback routing to a smaller variant for timeouts. We'll measure impact on unit cost.

Action items and owners
- Redwood (Soji) — deliver prompt set + initial benchmark run by 2027-04-23.
- Marissa — own structured-output regression criteria and create CI eval harness (match/levenshtein thresholds) by 2027-04-26.
- ACME (Priya) — share 200 de-identified intake examples and current golden JSONs by 2027-04-22.

Attachments: acme_postcall_notes.pdf (this email's detailed notes), acme_prompt_set_v1.json, acme_schema_v2.json

If this looks right I’ll schedule a 45-min follow-up next week to run through a live demo of model outputs + failure cases.

Thanks —
Soojin

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed next steps (model fit + schema conformance)

Thanks, Soojin — this is very helpful. We'll get the de-identified intake examples over to you by EOD tomorrow (200 records). A few questions from our security/data team:

1) Any concerns about PII leaking into model outputs? We need a short summary of mitigation strategies (redaction + prefix filters + prompt-level instructions).
2) For the schema conformance tests: do you run soft validation (post-hoc repair) or strict rejection? We want to understand both behaviors and failure rates.

Also, the procurement person (Sam) is looping in asking whether we can sign a standard DPA + review an SLA draft before the demo.

Priya Singh
Product Lead — Patient Intake, ACME Health
priya@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 13:28:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: ACME eval plan items and CI hooks

Soojin/Monica —

Quick internal note following Priya's questions:
- PII mitigation: recommend two-layer approach — (1) preprocess redaction rules (PII regexes + custom entity recognizer) prior to sending to model; (2) postprocess validation against schema and a small repair step (JS-based field normalizer) for common formatting issues (dates, phone). Document both options to ACME (we can show tradeoffs).
- Schema conformance behavior: we should demonstrate three modes in the demo: strict (reject outputs that fail schema), repair (attempt auto-fix then accept), and function-call (model returns function args which we validate server-side). Capture rejection rate for each.
- CI eval harness: I can spin up a lightweight GH Actions job that runs the prompt set against the two candidate models, records per-field precision/recall, and fails if macro-recall drops >5% vs baseline. Will add this to the repo under /ci/evals/acme.

Related links: HubSpot HS-ACME-1543 (deal record). I’ll prepare a short readout deck for the demo.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@acmehealth.com>, Sam Walters <swalters@techprocure.io>

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 18:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed next steps (model fit + schema conformance)

Great — appreciate the quick turnaround, Priya. Two quick answers and next steps: 

PII mitigation summary (short)
- Pre-send redaction: implement client-side redaction using ACME's rules (we'll validate with your sample set).
- Prompt-level instructions: explicit "do not hallucinate" and field-by-field extraction templates in prompt_set_v1.
- Postprocess guardrails: strict schema validation and function-call fallback; if strict mode fails, we will provide a repair attempt and log original+repaired for audit.

Schema modes we'll demo (on the call)
- Strict reject: show outputs that fail schema and how we surface errors in the Console.
- Auto-repair: show automatic fixes for common issues (date normalization, number formats).
- Function-call path: model returns typed args to extract_patient_record(payload) — server validates and persists if it passes.

Logistics / next steps
- ACME: please upload the 200 de-identified examples to the shared Drive folder (link below) by 2027-04-23.
- Redwood: we will run the initial benchmark (titan-7b-q4 & llama3-13b-instruct) on your dataset and share p50/p95 latencies, per-field precision/recall, and schema pass-rate by 2027-04-26.
- Demo: propose Wed 2027-04-28 10:00-10:45 PT for the live run-through + Q&A. I’ll send a calendar invite pending confirmation.

Drive link (upload folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmarks/acme-20270421
